item.title: LA County Adopts Heat Action Plan as Extreme Temperatures Kill 200+ Annually
item.description: Los Angeles County officials unanimously approved a comprehensive Heat Action Plan to combat extreme heat that kills over 200 residents annually. The plan prioritizes cooling outdoor spaces, improving indoor environments, and expanding public education about heat risks.

item.title: Factory-built housing hasn’t taken off in California yet, but this year might be different
item.description: Factory-built housing could finally gain momentum in California. Learn what’s changing in 2026, key challenges, and why the industry may take off now.

item.title: California Politburo
item.description: Santa Monica Daily Press columnist examines why LA politicians avoid challenging Mayor Bass, while local Santa Monica council members vote in lockstep.

item.title: Gale warning, thunderstorms threaten LA-area coast as powerful winter storm bears down on California
item.description: Gale warnings and severe thunderstorms threaten the LA coast as a powerful winter storm brings heavy rain, strong winds and flooding risks.

item.title: City's Spring Recreation Guide Now Available
item.description: The City of Malibu's Spring 2026 Recreation Guide is now available online and will be mailed to residents the week of Feb. 9. Programs running March through May include swim lessons, wellness workshops, birding classes, and the 25th Annual Chumash Day Powwow.

item.title: SMC Opens Spring Dance Series With Free Master Classes
item.description: Santa Monica College launches its Spring Dance Series with free master classes. Learn from expert instructors and enjoy inspiring dance events.

item.title: Santa Monica Council Postpones Mills Act Review Despite Completed Study
item.description: The Santa Monica City Council voted 5-2 to delay reviewing the city's Mills Act historic preservation tax program despite staff having already completed a consultant study on potential reforms. The program offers property tax reductions for historic buildings.

item.title: Malibu Awards $415,000 in Grants for Education, Wildfire Preparedness
item.description: The Malibu City Council has approved $415,000 in General Fund grants to two nonprofit organizations, with $315,000 going to the Malibu Education Foundation and $100,000 to the Community Brigade for emergency preparedness.
